title: Core-banking domain knowledge prepared as candidates: decision topics, compliance tactics and regulation records, core platform product categories, recovery and availability passages and the posting method
preparedBy: Sol, AIW round 12 workstream K (drafted, not reviewed by a person)
authority: Candidate only. Nothing in this file is approved, released or active, and no runtime module reads it. A record becomes knowledge only when the four-eyes knowledge approver attaches its exact passage as a source (knowledge.source), writes its claim on that passage (knowledge.claim), a second person verifies the claim (knowledge.review), and the claim is released and pinned (knowledge.release, knowledge.activate), in a project or once for an organisation. Released, it is offered to the chapters by its shape (public/domain-knowledge.js); before, it informs no score, hard constraint, conformance result, draft, retrieval or lens reading.
sourcePolicy: A passage is held only where its exact text is in this repository: AIW's own method text (origin aiw-authored) or the SA Playbook text the structured pack holds (origin sa-playbook). No third-party passage is held, retrieved or hashed, and no rights were checked. Every regulation record and every product fact needs its passage from a real source (sourcesNeeded); a record with no held passage cannot become a claim until the approver attaches one. "located" says how a title and section were found: here, always from the drafter's reading, not confirmed, or not located.

passage.text:
Where is a balanced posting enforced, and how is a repeated instruction recognised?
Decide which component keeps the general ledger and checks that each posting's debits equal its credits in each currency before it is committed; how each posting carries a reference unique to its originator, so that a repeated instruction posts once; and how a posted entry is corrected only by a reversing entry. Compare one posting service that every product calls with posting inside each product module, against the integrity, availability and performance drivers.
passage.licence: AIW-authored method text written for this pack; it copies no third-party text.

claim.statement: Decide which component keeps the general ledger and checks that each posting's debits equal its credits in each currency before it is committed; how each posting carries a reference unique to its originator, so that a repeated instruction posts once; and how a posted entry is corrected only by a reversing entry. Compare one posting service that every product calls with posting inside each product module, against the integrity, availability and performance drivers.
conditions: A core-banking design that has to decide posting integrity.
limitations: It frames the decision and what to compare; it chooses nothing and states no value.
tags: question:Where is a balanced posting enforced, and how is a repeated instruction recognised?

passage.text:
What runs at end of day, in what order and window, and what stays online?
Decide the end-of-day window, the posting cut-off and how the business date rolls; the order of the steps and which step waits for which; how a failed step restarts without posting twice; and which services stay online during the run and which date their postings take. Compare a run that stops posting with an online end of day in which postings after the cut-off take the next business date, against the availability and operability drivers.
passage.licence: AIW-authored method text written for this pack; it copies no third-party text.

claim.statement: Decide the end-of-day window, the posting cut-off and how the business date rolls; the order of the steps and which step waits for which; how a failed step restarts without posting twice; and which services stay online during the run and which date their postings take. Compare a run that stops posting with an online end of day in which postings after the cut-off take the next business date, against the availability and operability drivers.
conditions: A core-banking design that has to decide end of day.
limitations: It frames the decision and what to compare; it chooses nothing and states no value.
tags: question:What runs at end of day, in what order and window, and what stays online?

passage.text:
Which actions need a second person, and where is that enforced?
Decide which transactions and which changes to parameters, users and limits need a checker; where the rule is enforced: one approval service, or each module; how approval limits route an item and where it escalates; and how one person is kept from both entering and approving the same item. Compare a central workflow with approvals built into each module, against the security, traceability and operability drivers.
passage.licence: AIW-authored method text written for this pack; it copies no third-party text.

Compare a central workflow with approvals built into each module, against the security, traceability and operability drivers.
conditions: A core-banking design that has to decide approval workflow.
limitations: It frames the decision and what to compare; it chooses nothing and states no value.
tags: question:Which actions need a second person, and where is that enforced?

passage.text:
How are products and their parameters defined, dated and changed?
Decide where products and their parameters (rates, tariffs, limits, fees) are defined; how a change is dated so that past transactions keep the values that applied to them; who approves a change before it takes effect; and whether a new product needs a software release. Compare a product factory that every module reads with parameters held in each module, against the maintainability and integrity drivers.
passage.licence: AIW-authored method text written for this pack; it copies no third-party text.

claim.statement: Decide where products and their parameters (rates, tariffs, limits, fees) are defined; how a change is dated so that past transactions keep the values that applied to them; who approves a change before it takes effect; and whether a new product needs a software release. Compare a product factory that every module reads with parameters held in each module, against the maintainability and integrity drivers.
conditions: A core-banking design that has to decide product parameters.
limitations: It frames the decision and what to compare; it chooses nothing and states no value.
tags: question:How are products and their parameters defined, dated and changed?

passage.text:
How are amounts held in several currencies, valued and revalued?
Decide how every amount carries its currency; where exchange rates come from and which rate applies to a transaction; how a cross-currency posting balances in each currency; and when foreign balances are revalued and where the gains and losses are posted. Compare one ledger with currency position accounts with a ledger per currency, against the integrity and reporting drivers.
passage.licence: AIW-authored method text written for this pack; it copies no third-party text.

claim.statement: Decide how every amount carries its currency; where exchange rates come from and which rate applies to a transaction; how a cross-currency posting balances in each currency; and when foreign balances are revalued and where the gains and losses are posted. Compare one ledger with currency position accounts with a ledger per currency, against the integrity and reporting drivers.
conditions: A core-banking design that has to decide currencies.
limitations: It frames the decision and what to compare; it chooses nothing and states no value.
tags: question:How are amounts held in several currencies, valued and revalued?

passage.text:
How is each regulatory return produced from the ledger and reconciled to it?
Decide which returns are due, to which authority and by when; from which records each return is built and how its totals reconcile to the ledger; which returns are produced automatically and which by hand; and who checks a return before it is submitted. Compare returns built from a reporting store refreshed from the ledger with returns built from extracts, against the compliance and traceability drivers.
passage.licence: AIW-authored method text written for this pack; it copies no third-party text.

claim.statement: Decide which returns are due, to which authority and by when; from which records each return is built and how its totals reconcile to the ledger; which returns are produced automatically and which by hand; and who checks a return before it is submitted. Compare returns built from a reporting store refreshed from the ledger with returns built from extracts, against the compliance and traceability drivers.
conditions: A core-banking design that has to decide regulatory reporting.
limitations: It frames the decision and what to compare; it chooses nothing and states no value.
tags: question:How is each regulatory return produced from the ledger and reconciled to it?

passage.text:
Where may customer data live, and how is it kept there?
Decide in which country or region customer data must stay; which zones, providers and backups may hold it; how personal data is protected in transit, at rest and outside production; and what a provider outside the boundary may receive. Compare holding the data in the country with a provider's region, against the residency constraint and the availability and cost drivers.
passage.licence: AIW-authored method text written for this pack; it copies no third-party text.

claim.statement: Decide in which country or region customer data must stay; which zones, providers and backups may hold it; how personal data is protected in transit, at rest and outside production; and what a provider outside the boundary may receive. Compare holding the data in the country with a provider's region, against the residency constraint and the availability and cost drivers.
conditions: A core-banking design that has to decide data residency.
limitations: It frames the decision and what to compare; it chooses nothing and states no value.

passage.text:
Keep a register of the obligations that apply to the platform, each naming its regulator, instrument and section.
Map each obligation to the design records that meet it and to the tests or reports that show it is met.
When an obligation changes, open the records it maps to for review.
passage.licence: AIW-authored method text written for this pack; it copies no third-party text.

claim.statement: Keep a register of the obligations that apply to the platform, each naming its regulator, instrument and section. Map each obligation to the design records that meet it and to the tests or reports that show it is met. When an obligation changes, open the records it maps to for review.
conditions: The platform is subject to named regulation or contractual obligations.
limitations: The register shows where an obligation is met; it does not interpret the law, and a person who can name the jurisdiction keeps it current.

passage.text:
Hold regulatory parameters (limits, thresholds, customer tiers, retention periods, reporting dates) as configuration with an effective date.
Change them under maker-checker, never in code, so that a past transaction keeps the values that applied to it.
passage.licence: AIW-authored method text written for this pack; it copies no third-party text.

claim.statement: Hold regulatory parameters (limits, thresholds, customer tiers, retention periods, reporting dates) as configuration with an effective date. Change them under maker-checker, never in code, so that a past transaction keeps the values that applied to it.
conditions: Regulation sets values the platform must apply, and they change over time.
limitations: It says where the values live and how they change, not what they are: each value comes from the instrument that sets it.

records.title: Evidence from the platform's own records

passage.text:
Produce the evidence that an obligation is met from records the platform already keeps: the audit history, the reconciled ledger, the approval records.
Produce it on request and for a period, rather than assembling it by hand.
passage.licence: AIW-authored method text written for this pack; it copies no third-party text.

claim.statement: Produce the evidence that an obligation is met from records the platform already keeps: the audit history, the reconciled ledger, the approval records. Produce it on request and for a period, rather than assembling it by hand.
conditions: An auditor, a regulator or a customer may ask for evidence that an obligation is met.
limitations: The evidence is only as good as the records: an audit history that can be changed proves nothing.
tags: name:Evidence from the platform's own records

records.title: Returns reconciled to the ledger before submission

passage.text:
Build each regulatory return from the ledger, or from a reporting store refreshed from it.
Reconcile the return's totals to the ledger before it is submitted, and keep the reconciliation with the return.
passage.licence: AIW-authored method text written for this pack; it copies no third-party text.

claim.statement: Build each regulatory return from the ledger, or from a reporting store refreshed from it. Reconcile the return's totals to the ledger before it is submitted, and keep the reconciliation with the return.
conditions: The platform submits regulatory returns built from its records.
limitations: Which returns are due, and their format, come from the regulator's own rules.
tags: name:Returns reconciled to the ledger before submission

records.title: Core banking platform
records.holds: A packaged platform that keeps customer accounts, deposits and loans, the general ledger, interest and charges, and end-of-day processing.
factsNeeded: Which products and account types it holds (current and savings accounts, term deposits, loans).
Whether it keeps the general ledger itself or posts to an external one.
Which day-count bases and interest methods it supports, and how accruals are posted.
How it holds amounts in several currencies and revalues foreign balances.
Its end-of-day model: what stops, what stays online, and how the business date rolls.
How products and parameters are configured, and whether a new product needs a software release.
Its maker-checker controls and audit history.
The deployment and operating models offered (on premises, hosted by the provider, as a service), and the regions where data may be held.
The versions supported, the upgrade path and how often upgrades are required.
How it is licensed, and what leaving it would take (data export, contract terms).

records.title: Availability: what it is traded against

passage.text:
Cost: High availability solutions often require more expensive infrastructure, software licenses, and operational overhead.
Complexity: Highly available systems can be more complex to design, develop, and manage.

Security: Balancing high availability with strong security can be challenging, as some security measures may impact performance or availability.

records.title: Idempotent posting boundary
records.lineage: Generalised from the Bank Payment reference's decision ADR-002, Where should one financial effect be enforced? (public/decisions-domain.js), where the core ledger stands behind an external party; here the ledger is the system's own.

passage.text:
The core ledger is part of the system under design, and its posting operation is the boundary where one financial effect is enforced.
Every instruction carries a reference that its originator keeps for every retry.
The ledger records that reference with the posting in the same transaction, so a repeated instruction finds the recorded posting and returns its result instead of posting again.
A check made outside that transaction, such as a cache of recent references, only saves work; it is never the guarantee.
passage.licence: AIW-authored method text written for this pack; it copies no third-party text.

claim.statement: The core ledger is part of the system under design, and its posting operation is the boundary where one financial effect is enforced. Every instruction carries a reference that its originator keeps for every retry. The ledger records that reference with the posting in the same transaction, so a repeated instruction finds the recorded posting and returns its result instead of posting again. A check made outside that transaction, such as a cache of recent references, only saves work; it is never the guarantee.
conditions: A posting may be requested more than once: by a retry, after a timeout, or as a repeated message.
limitations: The reference must be unique to its originator and kept for as long as a retry can arrive.
It does not say what to do when an outcome is unknown: enquire before retry does.

records.title: Enquire before retry
records.lineage: Generalised from the Bank Payment reference's decision ADR-003, What should happen after an uncertain settlement response? (public/decisions-domain.js), where the core ledger stands behind an external party; here the ledger is the system's own.

passage.text:
When a call that may have changed a balance does not answer in time, its outcome is unknown, not failed.
Keep the instruction pending with its original reference.
Ask the side that may have applied it for the outcome, by a status enquiry or at the next reconciliation, and replay only when it is shown not to have been applied, with the same reference.
Until then, report the instruction as pending.

claim.statement: When a call that may have changed a balance does not answer in time, its outcome is unknown, not failed. Keep the instruction pending with its original reference. Ask the side that may have applied it for the outcome, by a status enquiry or at the next reconciliation, and replay only when it is shown not to have been applied, with the same reference. Until then, report the instruction as pending.
conditions: A call that may change a balance can end without an answer.
limitations: It needs the other side to answer an enquiry or to report what it applied; without either, the outcome stays unknown until a person investigates.
The time an instruction may stay pending is the project's to state.
